q: Can a foreigner set up a company in Singapore?
a: Singapore is very welcoming to foreigners who want to incorporate. Foreigners can become directors and shareholders here without any restrictions. Each local company must have at least one resident director when setting up their business: a Singapore national or a Permanent Resident. To comply with this requirement, you can hire a nominee director.

q: How do I register a company in Singapore?
a: Choose your company name and business activity, and provide details of the directors and shareholders. Our experts prepare your company constitution and incorporation documents, complete compliance checks, and submit your application to ACRA. Once your Unique Entity Number (UEN) is issued, your company is ready to operate.

q: How long does incorporation take?
a: Most companies are incorporated in 1 to 3 business days once all required documents are received. The most important factor is collecting all the documents. Keep in mind that the authorities only process registrations during working hours, and some business activities may require additional approval.

q: How does accounting work?
a: Accounting tracks all your business activities and assets. Whenever you spend, lose or make money, your bookkeeper adds it to your records. Your accountant then builds reports using these numbers. The government requests these reports to calculate how much tax you owe and whether you are exempted from some of it.

q: Why is accounting important?
a: First of all, you have an obligation to report your accounts to the government: that is how your tax is calculated. Secondly, accounting is crucial for internal planning and management. Mistakes could be costly: the government can fine business owners for inaccurate reports. Making sure your accounting is accurate is crucial.

q: What are the accounting standards in Singapore?
a: Singapore has its own system called Singapore Financial Reporting Standards (SFRS). It is similar to IFRS and it is accrual-based accounting. This means transactions are recognised when they occur and not when the money is paid. Outsourced accounting services in Singapore must comply with SFRS requirements.

q: Does every Singapore company need a company secretary?
a: Yes. A Singapore company must appoint a company secretary within six months of incorporation. The secretary must be ordinarily resident in Singapore and have the knowledge and experience necessary to carry out their duties. A sole director cannot also act as the company secretary.
